tasks.short: Hand out jobs to helpers, show them how to take apart and rebuild equipment, check their work, record parts cleaned and replaced, and update the planner on progress.

steps.what: Heavy equipment mechanic hands out jobs to helpers at the start of the shift
Heavy equipment mechanic directs workers who are assembling or disassembling equipment
Heavy equipment mechanic checks the helpers' work and settings
Helpers tick the parts they cleaned and replaced on the work order
Heavy equipment mechanic records which parts were cleaned and replaced: written down today; after the change the mechanic checks the helpers' ticks
Heavy equipment mechanic phones the planner about progress

tasks.design: Digital work orders on a workshop tablet ({OPS_SYSTEM}) list the tasks per machine, and the mechanic assigns them to helpers on screen. Helpers tick parts cleaned and replaced, so the mechanic only checks the list, and the planner sees progress from the work order status. Showing, directing and checking the work stay with the mechanic.
tasks.previous_blocker: Jobs were handed out verbally, parts noted on paper and progress phoned through.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital work orders run on tablets in workshops.
tasks.still_hard: Dirty hands and gloves make tablets awkward in the workshop.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a helper is about to lift a part the wrong way.

reach.learn: Whether live status cuts calls to the workshop.

evidence.claim: OutSmart covers work orders from job to invoice for installers.
Using work order time stamps to watch technician speed needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from work orders to progress shared; invoicing is outside.
Input contract: work orders from the planner; task lists set by the workshop lead; fallback is paper.

Directing and checking keep their full time. s1 keeps 85 because helpers see their tasks on the tablet and the mechanic still explains each job; s4 keeps 50 for checking and correcting the ticks; s5 keeps 40 for calls about delays.
Helpers' time is outside the mechanic's savings; their ticks are step s3b (share 1, other role).
research_questions: Do planner calls to the workshop fall?

incremental.description: No new upkeep: checking the helpers' ticks is s4's remaining time.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: helpers often forget to tick, so the mechanic still writes most parts down and the planner still phones (5.9); high: helpers tick as designed (13.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The mechanic keeps directing and checking work; paper notes and progress calls shrink.
skills_to_grow: Assigning work on digital work orders
role.ambitious_version: A workshop where the planner sees progress without calling.

job.title: Mobile Heavy Equipment Mechanics, Except Engines
